title: Midyear Alignment Weekend — Field Guide & OKR Drafts
summary: Field-guide for an internal half-day alignment weekend focused on finalizing company OKRs for H2, prepping the exec update narrative, and running a polished all-hands run-of-show. This is a working doc — lots of TODOs and open questions. Primary goals: 1) lock top-level OKRs and lead owners, 2) agree comms narrative and data points for exec update, 3) rehearse slide handoffs and Q&A plan.
agenda: 09:20–10:05 OKR workshop (breakouts by functional clusters) — define KRs, owners, measurement
10:05–10:20 Break — quick sync in Miro board
10:20–11:00 Exec narrative + data review (CPO/CRO/CTO) — finalize slides and speaker notes
11:00–11:30 Run-of-show & dry run (slides + transitions) — full walkthrough
11:30–12:00 Q&A rehearsals + escalation protocol — pre-write answers to top 5 questions
12:00–12:15 Wrap, next steps, immediate action owners
okr_drafts:
OKR 1 — Make inference predictable and economical (Ownership: Marco Li, Eng-Serving)
KR1.1: Improve 95th percentile inference latency on hosted API by 20% for 8k context workloads (baseline: 320ms) — metric owner: infra/perf
KR1.2: Reduce hosted per-token cost for the median workload by 15% via batching + KV caching recommendations deployed to top-10 customers — metric owner: optimize
KR1.3: Publish 3 validated quantization profiles with end-to-end perf/quality tradeoffs for Dedicated customers — metric owner: applied-ml

OKR 2 — Expand Dedicated & Private revenue motion (Ownership: Priya Desai, GTM)
KR2.1: Close 6 new Dedicated contracts (monthly committed capacity >= $50k) — sales
KR2.2: Ship VPC onboarding path with self-serve checklist and one-click KMS integration — product & infra
KR2.3: Reduce time-to-production for Private trials from 10 days to 4 days (measure: trial start -> first sustained inference traffic) — solutions engineering

OKR 3 — Developer velocity & platform observability (Ownership: Jonah Park, DevExp + Console)
KR3.1: Launch token-level cost explorer + per-route latency heatmap with 90-day retention for paid tiers — product
KR3.2: Reduce average incident-to-resolution time for inference degradations by 30% through runbooks + playbooks — SRE
KR3.3: Ship 4 SDK integrations and 6 reference apps demonstrating best-practice batching + caching patterns — devx
exec_update_draft:
Three themes to lead with: 1) Serving economics and reliability (what customers feel today, where we will be before year-end); 2) Go-to-market momentum for Dedicated & Private (tractable ARR targets and ramp plan); 3) Developer-first product commitments (console observability + SDKs).

CEO talking points (3–4 min):
- Quick state: product-market fit for inference: healthy growth, early enterprise traction, signal from top customers on latency/cost.
- Big bet: 'We win by being the predictable inference layer' — highlight recent infra wins (batching KV cache, kernel optimizations), a topline performance stat, and an anecdote from a customer that lowered token spend by X%.

CPO talking points (4–5 min):
- What we will deliver this quarter: token explorer, rollouts improvements, canary/fallback policies.
- Data snapshot: adoption of streaming & function-calling; top 5 feature requests.

CRO talking points (3 min):
- Sales traction and Enterprise pipeline highlights; quick case study (one Dedicated customer onboarding story).

Close: call-to-action for the org (3 asks) and rally phrase for H2.

Open notes: need up-to-date metrics from product analytics and a one-paragraph customer quote. Who can secure HQ metrics by EOD Friday?
allhands_run_of_show: 00:00–03:00 Intro (CEO) — slide 1–3, poll: ‘what matters most to you — latency, cost, or reliability?’
03:00–10:00 Product strategy (CPO) — slide 4–12, demo token explorer (live) — fallback prepared if live demo flaky
15:00–18:00 Engineering wins (VP Eng) — slide 18–22, short technical highlight from serving-runtime team
18:00–24:00 Roadmap commitments & OKRs (Head of Product Ops) — slide 23–30, outline measurement plan
24:00–30:00 Q&A (panel) — pre-seeded questions then live questions, escalation plan if sensitive topics appear
rehearsal_notes:
- Aim for slide transitions less than 5s.
- Speaker cue card: 1–2 bullets, not full script.
- Demo fallbacks: a) recorded video, b) step-through screenshots, c) synthetic load chart.
- Q&A prewrite: have answers to billing/security/region-support questions.
- AV checks: joint with SRE 30m before start.
- Timekeeper: Eleni will signal with 30s, 10s warnings (use Slack #allhands-run channel).
risks: Live demo fails (mitigation: recorded demo + screenshots ready)
Disagreement on KR measurability across teams (mitigation: bring measurement owners to final workshop)
Missing up-to-date metrics (mitigation: analytics runbook owner to export dashboards by Thu)
Too many OKRs (mitigation: prioritize top 3 company-level + 6 org-level)
Sensitive customer feedback surfaces in Q&A (mitigation: escalate to CRO + Comms, canned response templates)

open_questions: Do we keep three company OKRs or collapse to two? Pros/cons for investor narrative vs focus.
Which Dedicated deal (candidate list) do we highlight as the case study? Need permission from customer for quote.
Slack poll for all-hands engagement: live Q&A vs anonymous questions — which yields better signal?
Should we announce a new optimize feature in the same all-hands or wait for dedicated baseline tests?
notes_to_self: This doc is intentionally messy — the goal is to capture decision context. After alignment weekend we should: 1) move finalized OKRs to Confluence, 2) create a public-facing all-hands deck, 3) spin up measurement trackers in Looker and assign watchers.
